Engaging Deck Builder with Narrative Depth I found this title to be a refreshing addition to the genre. Drawing parallels to the popular Slay the Spire, this game offers a narrative-driven experience that initially captivates the player's attention. The storytelling is compelling, with each run providing a unique opportunity to uncover more about the game world. However, being a rogue-lite game, the repetition of dialogue and story beats can become tiresome after multiple playthroughs. Constantly mashing the skip button to bypass familiar conversations detracts from the overall enjoyment. Despite this minor setback, the core mechanics shine brightly. The strategic depth of deck-building is fully realized here, requiring careful planning and adaptation to overcome each challenge. Additionally, the inclusion of allies with their own specialized spells adds an extra layer of complexity and excitement to the gameplay. Overall, while the narrative aspect may lose its luster over time, the engaging gameplay mechanics ensure that every run feels fresh and rewarding. Fans of deck-building games will find plenty to love here, making it a worthy addition to their library.

挺好玩的，2024年第一款令人快乐的肉鸽卡游。与其说是杀塔其实更像欺诈之地，你的选择能左右剧情分支。配音美术和音乐都为上乘。目前体感数值设计比较合理，难度适中。支持语种暂时只有英文和葡萄牙语，不介意的话推荐入手。 这边列一下我个人比较在意的小问题: - 支持语言过少，有个别未翻译的UI(即使选择英文仍是葡萄牙语)。 - 虽然美工很好，但是UI（尤其键位的设置）有点奇怪。比如确定键是空格，回合结束是shift等等。玩家在玩其他类似游戏时会有肌肉记忆，在这个游戏里很容易按错键。 - 鼠标的移动感觉不是很灵活，查看技能时经常直接选取了不想要的卡牌。 - 战斗不支持2倍速。因为打完一整轮会要很久时间，能压缩下战斗动画耗时感觉还是挺必要的。 - 事件会带来什么收益/后果很不清晰，经常触发不想要的结果。 - Roll卡判定挺毒的，因为删除诅咒卡的手段来得非常晚，导致随机事件的风险和回报不成正比。希望把判定稍微改松一点，哪怕是一张卡的区别都会大幅提升收益和体验。 总体来说瑕不掩瑜，希望开发组接下来能够积极更新。 ---------------------------------------------------------------------- 又通了几次，熟练工的话不刷金块大概一周目接近3小时。成型毕竟容易，成型之后Act3一路爽杀，而且卡组不是太薄。但愿后续能更新一些增加难度的选项。

For everyone who doesn't understand why this game is receiving positive feedback on Steam: the reason is that it was developed by a very famous media group in Brazil, using an IP that is very dear to the hearts of many Brazilian nerds, and that's pretty much it. To be honest, I don't think the price is justifiable, considering the overall quality of the game. It is not indie by any means, being funded and produced by one of the biggest corporations in Latin America. The quantity of bugs and the visible simplicity of many animations, along with the barebones card game system, all point to a very inexperienced group of developers who didn't test the game enough. As a fan of Jovem Nerd and a reader of Ruff Ghanor, I cannot recommend this game at its current price. It's a simple mobile game with simplistic systems and incomplete premises. You cannot fully enjoy the rich story of the Ruff Ghanor IP, delve into complex game mechanics, or appreciate artistic mastery in any way. I hope that the sequel receives the well-deserved treatment that this IP deserves.

Changed my review from positive to negative because theres an unacceptable amount of crashing and bricking for a released version of the game. Game also relies way way too much on memorization, You basically get dialogue options and you have to know what to pick or else you might be penalized. Making players memorize answers is not an acceptable gameplay mechanic lmao. Pros - Has decent lore - Good art + battle animations - Has a direction that seperates it from other deck builders Cons - Feels like there are some balancing issues, because you have to memorize events because too many curse cards will f you, first troll + skele boss can be somewhat hard also without a certain style build. Lacks healing source on C1, you either have to use your card slots for Cures and you have to rely on others to cure. Especially early when you still havent memorized events. - Unlocking new card slots is slow - Has a stacking punishing card system and you cant remove the cards at card removal events (which are decently rare also) feels terrible, relies on memorization + RNG, bad combo - Half of the cards are just copy pasta from other deckbuilder games - Game price high esp compared to quality - some crashing + bricking - Story becomes somewhat cringe upon finishing C2 Also: 1: I dont want to do 2 button presses on the skip tutorial screen because the active button is defaulted to be on the tutorial button). unnecessary clicks. 2: the forge system is again, unnecessarily complicated/too many clicks, make changing cards simple with less clicks. 3: The events become a memory game at some point and punishing for that is plain stupid when you cant even remove curses 4: With a Discard card, if I click on a card to discard and I want to change my mind, for gods sake let me just click another card and not have to unclick the first card first. 5: Give option to disable miracle scroll animations completely 6: Theres a bug if your character dies after last enemy dies, it continues the game with you at 0 HP and bricks your file 7: Alot of crashes. Crash on loading screen can brick your save file. 8: One can abuse closing the client and restarting to get another try on a fight, might be able to abuse on curse card events unsure. 9: Dwarf forge event is somewhat confusing and you can accidently go through with the crafting by accident Could have made the game alot better with small changes and less bugs 7/10 deckbuilder game

Sad to review it negatively, I was so excited to play it and had some fun. However the devs completely abandoned the game in the worst state possible. The first build worked on SteamDeck. Several crashes and compatibility problems, but it was possible to play. The last build, however, broke completely. It just can't run anymore. And the fact that it's been a while since it got out and no other movement happened, I just can't recommend the game. And since I'm on it, as a game developer myself, I can't imagine what justified this game being made in Unreal Engine. It's a 2D UI game, literally any other engine/tool could have been a better choice. I mean that because Unreal is such big and complicated engine. Look at other games like Balatro, for example, one that I'd consider in the same category, it was made using Löve, a simple (yet quite powerful) framework in Lua. So you get to develop the whole game in a much more simple programming language that will yield much less bugs due its simplicity. As a result, Balatro was made probably in less time, by less people, with less money, and is a much better game, but not only because its gameplay mechanics, but also because of what the tooling allowed the developers to focus on. I don't mean to insult the developers, quite the opposite, I'm pretty sure they worked hard to get this game out, as they probably were the people who liked it the most. And for this I actually congratulate them for making the best they could. I am sure this is a problem with upper management. The ones who decide usually don't know anything about the craft and this is possibly a case of how bad technical decisions can absolutely ruin a project.

Feels like a mobile game, there are bugs and even enemy intent isn't (clearly) communicated. Also companions have act separately after the other's turn is finished, and you won't see the companion's deck until it is their turn, so all the talk about synergies and what not will not be true. You don't share the mana pool either. Lots of weird decisions and the writing is not very good either, to be blunt.

Do not recommend. After a couple runs I decided to look into the comments to see if I was just bad or the game was unbalanced, and the comments confirmed it for me. You can get through the first several encounters just fine but once the map starts getting messy it's impossible to know the difficulty of your next battle. I was faced with impossible odds on each run and it seemed like my tactical decisions throughout the game made little difference one way or another. After a failed run you get to keep your gold but I could never save enough to buy anything good that could help because it costs way too much to build my deck in any meaningful way. I end up spending my whole savings just removing one or two cards and am stuck with any other crappy ones that don't fit my strategy. This makes your hands watered down and ineffective at best, and absolutely frustrating and useless at worst. If the developers could fix the balance of the game I could leave a positive review.

ABANDONWARE WITH BUGS I wanted to rate this positive, but although the issues can be fixed and the game overall is ok, it seems abandoned. Bugs: I've faced about 1 fatal error after every event on end of act 2 for some reason. annoying as fk. unbalanced gameplay: you either luck out or its a no go run. i tried 3 times, 2 times i couldnt finish act 1. third time i got a relic that healed me everytime i consumed. There is a card that consumes and makes another consumable, and that one remakes the first consume card. infinite loop, that card alone got me from act 1 to game end without any issues. no skills attached, just pure luck. BAD design on the events: we dont know what option will reward us with what and roleplaying doesnt mean anything. choices do not matter. solid 6/10 game, so a reluctant thumbs down unless the dev fix the bugs.
